title: Chapter 3 Quiz 15
description: Traps in every question. Read each loop line by line and do not trust the first impression.
instructions: Chapter 3: Difficult: loops and hidden errors.
Take your time: read each question carefully, then check your answer.

questions.question: This should display the smallest of the 5 values in tab. Two lines have an error.
questions.code:
Let min ← 0
For i From 1 To 5 Do
    If tab[i] > min Then
        min ← tab[i]
    EndIf
EndDo
Display(min)
questions.explanation: Line 1: min must start with the first element, tab[1]. Line 3: we replace min when the new value is smaller, so the test is tab[i] < min. Watch out: starting at 0 fails when every value is positive, and > finds the largest value.

questions.question:
How many times does the body run?
```
For i From 1 To 4 Do
    For j From i To 4 Do
        Display(i, j)
    EndDo
EndDo
```
questions.explanation: i = 1 gives 4 passes, i = 2 gives 3, i = 3 gives 2 and i = 4 gives 1. The total is 4 + 3 + 2 + 1 = 10. Watch out: the inner loop starts at i, not at 1.
questions.hint: The inner loop starts at i, not at 1.

questions.question:
How many numbers does this algorithm display?
```
Let i ← 3
Repeat
    Display(i)
    i ← i - 1
Until i <= 0
```
questions.explanation: It displays 3, 2 and 1. When i becomes 0 the test is true and the loop stops. Watch out: 0 is never displayed, because the test comes after the display and i is changed before the test.

questions.question: Trace this loop: i ← 25, then While i > 3 Do i ← i - 7. Fill in the table.
questions.explanation: 25 → 18 → 11 → 4 → -3. Watch out: after pass 3, i = 4 and 4 > 3 is still true, so there is a fourth pass. i can end below zero.

questions.question: This should display the sum 1 + 2 + ... + n. One line is wrong. Find it and choose the fix.
questions.code:
Read(n)
Let total ← 0
For i From 1 To n - 1 Do
    total ← total + i
EndDo
Display(total)
options: For i From 1 To n + 1 Do
For i From 1 To n Do
For i From 0 To n Do
For i From 2 To n Do
questions.explanation: The last value, n, must be included. Watch out: To n - 1 stops one value too early, and From 0 or To n + 1 would change the result.

questions.question: This loop should display the even numbers from 1 to 5, then stop. One line is in the wrong place.
questions.code:
Let i ← 1
While i <= 5 Do
    If i MOD 2 = 0 Then
        Display(i)
        i ← i + 1
    EndIf
EndDo
questions.explanation: The increase of i must happen on every pass, so it belongs after EndIf. Watch out: inside the If it only runs for even numbers, so with i = 1 the loop never ends.

questions.question:
How many times does the body run?
```
For i From 2 To 20 Step 4 Do
    Display(i)
EndDo
```
questions.explanation: i takes 2, 6, 10, 14, 18. The next value, 22, is above 20. Watch out: 20 is not reached with a step of 4.

questions.question: Which of these statements are **true**?
options: A While loop tests its condition after the first pass
For i From 5 To 1 does not run when the step is +1
A Repeat loop whose Until test starts true still runs once
A While loop whose test is false at the start runs 0 times
For i From 1 To 0 runs the body exactly one time
questions.explanation: While tests first (0 times is possible). A For loop with the start above the end does not run. Repeat...Until always runs once before testing. Watch out: For i From 1 To 0 is an empty range, and While never tests after the body.

questions.question: A program must ask for numbers until the user types 0, and the user may type 0 straight away. Which structure fits best?
questions.explanation: Read first, then test, so a first 0 does no work. Watch out: with Repeat...Until the first 0 would be processed as if it were a value.

questions.question: Evaluate each expression (the brackets show the order).
questions.explanation: 17 MOD 5 = 2 and 17 DIV 5 = 3; 20 DIV 3 = 6 and 20 MOD 3 = 2. Watch out: DIV gives the quotient and MOD the remainder, and they are easy to swap.

questions.assertion: In For i From 1 To N, when N = 0 the body runs once.
questions.reason: The initial and final values of a For loop are both included.
questions.explanation: The assertion is false: the range 1 to 0 is empty, so the body does not run. Watch out: the reason is true, but it does not make the assertion hold.
